why_promising: The 2000 remedy amendment required investigation of existing cover thickness using a representative grid approach.
Areas with less than two feet of cover were to be upgraded with low-permeability soil and a six-inch erosion layer.
The landfill is approximately forty acres and therefore large enough in principle.
fatal_evidence: The 2025 Five-Year Review reports ponding, subsidence and increasingly large stands of woody vegetation on the landfill cover.
Areas of subsidence were repaired on two occasions and continued cover monitoring is ongoing.
The current source-control remedy and additional alternatives remain under evaluation.
The repaired and changing surface means the original grid-defined cover conditions cannot be treated as intact stable Sentinel-1-era depth zones.
sources_reviewed: EPA current Keystone Sanitation Landfill site profile
next_action: Continue the approved search unchanged and reject any historical cover grid whose mapped zones were later repaired, regraded, wooded or otherwise altered during the Sentinel-1 period.
